Leaves IndexedDB schema, migration versioning, home-room/snapshot store persistence, and the ledger's spend semantics to the client-storage/migration reviewer.

Does not re-litigate the sprite art content, palette choices, or aesthetic decisions from Tasks 1–2 (settled design/authoring work) — reviews only how what's authored gets sized, scaled, drawn, and captured on screen.
decision_lens: Does the canvas's backing store still match its CSS size, and does a tap still land on the room the player meant, after a resize, a pan, an async photo load, and hundreds of ticks of full-scene redraw — or only in the plan's own fixed-viewport, no-rotation motion sweep?
focus: Whether the single-canvas, integer-scaled, pixel-art rendering approach (Task 6's HouseCanvas, Task 7's rAF/register wiring, Task 13's offscreen drawRoomTo reuse) actually holds a legible, non-blurry, non-janky picture on real phone and desktop viewports at the stated redraw cadence, and whether the plan's own acceptance checks (image-smoothing count, integer scale, scale floor) are sufficient to catch the visual and performance failure modes a canvas-based cross-section like this is prone to.
name: fd-canvasgfx-viewportperf
persona: Apply the perspective of a graphics engineer who has shipped Canvas 2D pixel-art rendering pipelines for web games — integer-scale rendering, device-pixel-ratio handling, ResizeObserver-driven layout, offscreen capture, and mobile viewport/frame-budget engineering.
review_areas: Task 6 Step 1's scale formula S = max(scaleFloor ?? 2, floor(min(availW * dpr / LW, availH * dpr / LH))): on a tall/narrow phone viewport with a multi-room house (cols=2, rows growing per Task 3's grid rule as rooms are founded), verify the floor of 2 doesn't force the canvas's CSS size past the yard's available height/width once enough rooms are founded, and that Task 6 specifies what triggers the camera to re-center on new content (a newly founded room, a walking figure) versus leaving a player's manual pan position stranded off-frame.

Task 6 Step 3's tap-to-cell mapping ("onPointerUp maps CSS coordinates to a cell") combined with Step 1's camera-pan translate: confirm the coordinate mapping accounts for the pan offset and any ResizeObserver-driven S/canvas-size change (a resize firing between pointerdown and pointerup, or after a pan) — a stale scale or offset captured at pointerdown but not re-read at pointerup would make taps land on the wrong room after any resize or pan mid-gesture.

Task 6 Step 2's full-building redraw once per tick (TICK_MS=100, ~10 draws/sec), where every registered draw(walk) call redraws every room's wall, floor, window, frames, things, doors, stairs, figures, and tint: at a founded house with many rooms, this redraws the entire multi-room scene from scratch 10x/second even when nothing visible changed (no walker mid-transit, no door open) — assess whether this is a real frame-budget risk on lower-end mobile hardware, and whether Task 9's motion sweep (390×844 and 1300×800, discrete correctness checks only) is positioned to catch dropped frames or jank at all.

Task 13 Step 4's offscreen capture ("draw the room via drawRoomTo into an offscreen canvas at scale 3, toBlob, save... once per (dateKey, daypart)... nothing is captured when the tab is hidden"): verify drawRoomTo is guaranteed to draw from the same frame data the live canvas would show at that instant — since photos load asynchronously into an HTMLImageElement map (Task 7 Step 1), confirm a snapshot captured the instant a daypart's capture condition becomes true can't fire before that tick's photos finish loading, permanently freezing a blank photo frame into a write-once record.

AC 7 / Task 6 Step 2's photograph-smoothing scoping ("imageSmoothingEnabled = true for that call only"): AC 7 checks the literal string appears exactly once in HouseCanvas.tsx, but Task 13 adds a second canvas context (the offscreen capture canvas) that also draws photographs — verify that offscreen context gets its own smoothing toggle around its photo draw, since it's a different ctx than the live canvas's, and that AC 7's single-occurrence grep can't quietly pass while the snapshot's photos render wrong by omission.

Task 6 Step 1's ResizeObserver sizing and Task 7's rAF loop running independently per mount: confirm a resize (rotation, mobile browser-chrome show/hide on scroll, an on-screen keyboard opening) mid-session doesn't desync the canvas's backing-store pixel size from the CSS size it's drawn at — a classic canvas-DPR bug that reads as sudden blur or a stretched image — given the plan states no debouncing or ordering between the observer callback and the next draw() call.

severity_examples.condition: Triggered by any device rotation or mobile-chrome collapse event, which Task 9's motion sweep (fixed 390×844/1300×800, no rotation step) would never exercise, visibly breaking the integer-pixel-scale Must-Have.
severity_examples.scenario: The ResizeObserver-driven canvas resize (Task 6 Step 1) and the rAF-driven draw(walk) call (Task 7 Step 1) are two independent callbacks with no stated ordering guarantee; if a resize updates canvas.width/height without the same tick re-issuing ctx.setTransform and a redraw before the next paint, the browser presents a canvas whose backing store no longer matches its CSS size — every subsequent draw renders stretched or blurry pixel art until the next tick happens to catch up.

severity_examples.condition: Most likely on the same day a room is founded, since that's exactly when its anchor photo is newest and least likely to have finished loading before the day's snapshot moment fires.
severity_examples.scenario: drawRoomTo (Task 13) reuses the live canvas's per-room draw logic against a WalkState/HouseModel and a photos map that may still be mid-load for a room whose founding-anchor photo was just accepted that same daypart; the capture effect's only guard is "once per (dateKey, daypart)," not "once photos have loaded," so the write-once (add, ConstraintError swallowed) snapshot can freeze a blank photo frame into the record forever with no retry path.

severity_examples.condition: A mid-to-late-session house with many founded rooms could visibly stutter on real low-end phones without any acceptance criterion catching it before ship.
severity_examples.scenario: The full-scene redraw at 10Hz scales with total founded room count with no dirty-rectangle or partial-redraw strategy, and Task 9's motion/perf sweep checks visual correctness (doors, silhouettes, bubbles) but names no frame-rate or dropped-frame budget to pass or fail against.

success_hints: Anchors every finding to the specific Task 6, 7, or 13 step and the exact formula, prop, or AC (6, 7, 9) the plan states, quoting it, rather than general canvas-performance folklore.
Distinguishes a rendering-correctness bug (wrong pixels, wrong scale, wrong tap target) from a pure performance risk (frame budget, redraw cost) and states which for each finding.

Treats the plan's own acceptance checks (AC 7's single-occurrence grep, AC 9's integer-scale/scaleFloor grep) as string-matching proxies to be stress-tested for what they'd miss, not as settled proof the property holds everywhere it needs to.

Grounds mobile-viewport concerns in the actual devices/sizes the plan names (390×844, 1300×800, Task 9) plus real-world events the plan doesn't name (rotation, mobile chrome collapse, on-screen keyboard) rather than hypothetical unnamed devices.
Leaves walk-simulation determinism/pathfinding and IndexedDB schema/migration/concurrency to the other two reviewers; flags only what is drawn, scaled, captured, or mapped from screen coordinates.
